verdict.line: You lose if you trade into a fully-stacked Darkness Rise or eat a clean Death's Grasp; you win if you force fights right after his E whiffs or the instant your level 6/11 R comes online.

brief.thesis: Both champions are playing a stack-and-punish game: Mordekaiser needs Darkness Rise fully charged off Q/W/E hits before an auto becomes a free heal-and-burn, while Jax needs Grandmaster's Might (R) or a dodged Counter Strike (E) window to force a fight on his terms. Neither side has a hard structural edge — 50.8% over 520 games confirms it — so the lane is decided by who reads the other's cooldown/stack timer better, not by kit superiority.

theirWindow.when: His passive icon reads fully stacked
theirWindow.what: Disengage immediately instead of trading through it — his next auto heals him off the damage he just landed and adds bonus magic damage, which is exactly the 'retreat' trigger OP.GG is flagging.

yourWindow.when: Right after he whiffs Death's Grasp (E)
yourWindow.what: Walk in and start chaining Empower (W) autos immediately. His pull is now on a long cooldown, so he has no way to disengage or reset the trade until it comes back.

start.why: Highest-performing start (51.5% over 412 games, 62.2% pick) — the extra sustain and damage let you match his poke through level 2-3 instead of losing the HP race before your first back.

boots.why: Most-picked and best-performing boots (49.3% over 414 games, 69.4% pick) — tenacity blunts the Death's Grasp slow chain and the MR helps against a full-AP laner.

core.why: Part of the highest-winrate core path (58.7% over 46 games) — the Empower (W) proc scaling off Trinity is what turns your maxed-W trades into real damage from level 6 on.
Second item in the same 58.7% path — the on-hit proc and healing let you win the extended trades this matchup produces without falling behind on sustain.
Completes the top-performing measured path — lets you commit to all-ins inside his Realm of Death (R) without dying to the isolation burst.

runes.keystoneWhy: This is the majority page (40.8% pick, 49.8% wr) and fits the maxed-W, auto-heavy trade pattern this matchup produces — ramping attack speed rewards standing in and chaining Empower autos. If you'd rather lean into surviving his early poke instead of scaling, the Grasp of the Undying/Second Wind page (54.8% wr on a smaller 6.4%-pick sample) trades ceiling for lane sustain.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the most-picked (77%) and best-performing (51.5%) combo — Ignite cuts through the heal he gets from a fully-stacked Darkness Rise or his ultimate, turning close skirmishes into kills. Flash+Teleport (50.5%, 14.9% pick) is the alternative if you're prioritizing wave management and scaling into your item spikes over early kill pressure.

playing.title: Dodge Death's Grasp with movement
playing.detail: His E has a visible windup and a long cooldown once used — sidestep it rather than trading through it, since getting pulled locks you into full poke-and-auto range for the rest of the exchange.

playing.title: Track his passive stack fill
playing.detail: Darkness Rise stacks off his Q/W/E hits; once the icon reads full, his next auto heals him and adds bonus magic damage. This is the exact retreat trigger OP.GG calls out — break off before he lands that auto, not after.

playing.title: Use Counter Strike on his autos, not his spells
playing.detail: Counter Strike (E) only dodges incoming basic attacks — it does not stop Obliterate (Q) or Death's Grasp (E). Save it to punish him for last-hitting or trading autos, not as a defensive answer to his poke.

playing.title: All-in right at your level 6 spike
playing.detail: Grandmaster's Might (R) gives a guaranteed stun on your next attack plus bonus resistances and refreshes Counter Strike — from level 6-10 this wins straight fights even through one passive proc, so force it the moment he's used Q or E on a minion.

playing.title: Max W second for the trade pattern
playing.detail: The measured skill order maxes W right after E and Q (EQWWW...), so your empowered auto ramps fastest in damage and cooldown — lean on auto-W-auto trades from level 3-5 instead of forcing Q all-ins you can't yet win.

playing.title: Respect his ultimate, don't fear it
playing.detail: Realm of Death isolates you 1v1 with no outside interference, but the matchup data says this is even — don't commit to a long fight inside it unless your own E stun or R is already up.

playing.title: Freeze pre-6, shove post-6
playing.detail: Since the lane is a dead-even 50.8% over 520 games, wave state decides more fights than raw stats do — hold the freeze near your tower before level 6, then shove in to punish his passive falling off between engages once you have R.

brief.patchCaveat: The winrates, sample sizes, build order, rune pages, and summoner spell rates above are measured OP.GG data from real games on the current patch (16.18.1). The trade-pattern reasoning, cooldown windows, and skill-order justification explaining why those numbers look the way they do are my own tactical read.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being pulled by Death’s Grasp(E). Retreat if Mordekaiser’s passive ability activates.
